answer: New identities start in the lagoon, a pool of unpaid onboarding tasks. Each takes 15 minutes of real work and is checked by two peers. Ten clean finishes earn ten cedar credits. Claiming a paid task costs one credit, returned only when the task passes peer grading. Junk work burns the credit for good. A farm of 100 fakes must finish 1,000 onboarding tasks first — 250 hours of work, about $125 of rented compute at $0.50 an hour — and tasks arrive one per hour, so each clone needs 10 hours before its first paid task. The signal is simple: no history, no pay.
